strategy.summary: Commit 72802a9 (Show each line's product name on an order) made GET /orders/:id slower: the k6 `detail` scenario in perf/orders.js went from p95 22 ms to 30 ms and p99 23 ms to 31 ms, and a rerun confirmed it. The diff adds a third store query, `productNames`, after `orderLines`. It runs in sequence, so each detail request makes one more round trip of 6–9 ms. The guard adds `detail`-scoped p95 and p99 thresholds to perf/orders.js at the baseline plus 20%. It records the defect and files an issue for a person to fix.
inScope: perf/orders.js detail scenario: p95 and p99 latency thresholds tagged {scenario:detail}, added beside the existing ones (nothing else in the script changes)
Defect record and GitHub issue for the detail slowdown
outOfScope: Changing application code to win the time back (a person's fix)
perf/search.js search p99: the good runs vary too much to judge (cv 9.2%), not a confirmed slowdown; script left unchanged
assumptions: The thresholds use the baselines the work item gives (p95 22 ms, p99 23 ms) plus the 20% threshold: p(95)<26.4 and p(99)<27.6
The existing thresholds, checks and scenarios in perf/orders.js stay unchanged
TestForge's run_tests runs k6 with --no-thresholds and 1 iteration, so the counted runs prove the script runs. They don't show the threshold firing; that happens only under the script's own load
The app runs for real at BASE_URL (http://localhost:4310); nothing is faked

risks.description: Threshold set too tight could flake on a noisy CI runner
risks.mitigation: The detail baseline was stable (cv ~2%), and the threshold allows the full 20% headroom

risks.description: The threshold could hold the list scenario to detail's numbers

acceptanceCriteria.text: perf/orders.js fails under its own load when the detail scenario's p95 http_req_duration exceeds 26.4 ms (baseline 22 ms + 20%)
perf/orders.js fails under its own load when the detail scenario's p99 http_req_duration exceeds 27.6 ms (baseline 23 ms + 20%)

testCases.title: detail scenario keeps order detail p95 and p99 latency within the last good runs' level
steps: Run perf/orders.js under its own scenarios (20 req/s for 10 s per scenario)
k6 evaluates the 'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}' thresholds p(95)<26.4 and p(99)<27.6
testCases.expected: The thresholds fail while detail stays at p95 ~30 ms / p99 ~31 ms, and pass once it is back at the baseline
testCases.rationale: Guards the slowdown from 72802a9: app.js now awaits productNames() after orderLines(), a third sequential store round trip (6–9 ms) per order detail request, which matches the +8 ms at p95/p99

strategy.environmentNotes: The orders-api must be reachable at BASE_URL (default http://localhost:4310). TestForge's smoke run uses --no-thresholds.

defects.title: Order detail slowed by extra sequential productNames query (p95 22→30 ms)
defects.description: perf/orders.js › detail (GET /orders/:id): p95 latency went from 22 ms to 30 ms (+39.4%) and p99 from 23 ms to 31 ms (+36.2%) against the median of 5 good runs, and a rerun confirmed it. The bisect points to 72802a9fba0d "Show each line's product name on an order". In src/app.js the order route now awaits `productNames(...)` after `orderLines(order.id)`. That is a third store query in sequence, and each store query is one round trip of 6–9 ms (src/store.js roundTrip). The commit message says the names come "in one query with the lines", but they come from a separate query. Expected: detail p95 < 26.4 ms and p99 < 27.6 ms (baseline + 20%).
defects.evidence: k6 run perf/orders.js: http_req_duration{scenario:detail} p(95)=33.94ms ✗ 'p(95)<26.4', p(99)=37.54ms ✗ 'p(99)<27.6'; "thresholds on metrics 'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}' have been crossed"
